items.stem: A trader is told that initial margin on a futures contract is a 'down payment on ownership'. The correct characterisation is that margin is:

options.text: A performance bond ensuring the trader can meet obligations
options.rationale: Correct: futures margin is a good-faith performance bond, not equity ownership.
Margin is not a loan; it is a performance bond.
Margin can be returned when the position is closed in good standing.
Margin is a fraction of contract value, not the whole.

items.explanation: Correct: futures margin is a good-faith performance bond, not equity ownership.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A commercial producer wants to lock in a selling price for a crop it will harvest later. The most appropriate strategy is to:

options.text: Sell (short) futures contracts to hedge the expected output
options.rationale: Correct: a short hedge locks in a selling price for future output.

options.text: Buy call options with no underlying position
options.rationale: Buying calls does not lock in a selling price for output.
Unrelated speculation does not hedge the crop.

options.text: Do nothing and accept full price risk
options.rationale: Doing nothing leaves the producer fully exposed.

items.explanation: Correct: a short hedge locks in a selling price for future output.

items.stem: Before an associated person opens a futures account for a retail customer, which TWO are required or prohibited actions? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: risk disclosure is required before trading.

options.text: Avoid guaranteeing the customer against losses
options.rationale: Correct: guaranteeing against loss is a prohibited practice.

options.text: Promise specific profits to win the account
options.rationale: Promising profits is a prohibited sales practice.

items.explanation: Correct: risk disclosure is required before trading. Correct: guaranteeing against loss is a prohibited practice.
